Class KeyEvent

java.lang.Object
com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.input.KeyEvent
public class KeyEvent extends Object
Mutable key transition carrying both legacy LWJGL and native SDL identities.

Physical key presses are separate from Unicode text input. The character is normally zero except for legacy shortcut delivery; text arrives in FrameEvent.text. Instances are pooled by the frame buffer, so callers must not retain one across frames or use a changing instance as a hash-map key. Lombok supplies fluent accessors, all-field/no-argument constructors, and value-based equality.

    • KeyEvent

      public KeyEvent()
      Creates a reusable event with zero codes/character/modifiers and no pressed key.

    • KeyEvent

      public KeyEvent(int keyCode, char character, boolean pressed, int sdlKeyCode, int sdlScanCode, int sdlMod)
      Creates a new KeyEvent instance.
      Parameters:
      keyCode - LWJGL2-compatible key code used by Minecraft's legacy GUI callbacks.
      character - Legacy character, possibly zero; not the full composed Unicode text.
      pressed - True for key down, false for key up.
      sdlKeyCode - SDL layout-dependent key symbol associated with the transition.
      sdlScanCode - SDL layout-independent physical-key scancode.
      sdlMod - SDL modifier-bit snapshot captured at the time of the transition.

    • set

      public KeyEvent set(int keyCode, char character, boolean pressed)
      Reuses this object for the legacy half of a new transition. Native fields are intentionally untouched until setSdl(int, int, short) follows.
      Parameters:
      keyCode - LWJGL2-compatible code
      character - legacy shortcut character, or zero
      pressed - true for down, false for up
      Returns:
      this mutable event for chained population
